Pippit vs VEXI: Creative Tool or Your Whole Social Media?
Pippit makes videos, avatars and images and schedules them to TikTok, Facebook and Instagram. VEXI edits your own footage, designs, writes and posts.
Pippit is CapCut's sister app, with a publisher and a calendar. Here is how it compares with one app that makes your posts and runs your week.

Pippit is an AI creative tool "powered by CapCut". It turns a link, a file or media into videos, makes AI avatar and talking-photo videos, designs posters and social ads, and edits an uploaded clip when you type what you want. Its Publisher schedules posts on a social calendar to TikTok, Facebook and Instagram. There is a no-cost tier with daily credits; paid Starter, Plus and Pro plans are sold by monthly credits.

VEXI (formerly Social Realtr) is an AI content studio that runs social media for entrepreneurs and creators. You describe what you want and it makes the posts, videos, designs and captions, then schedules and publishes them. Plans start at $199 a month, and every plan starts with a 15-day trial.

Credit where it is due: Pippit makes a lot, and schedules it. The difference is who does the work. In Pippit you run each tool, add the stock clips and music, and fill the calendar yourself. VEXI does that: your own clips come back with B-roll, music and captions, the posts come back designed and captioned, and Autopilot runs your week. VEXI costs more than Pippit: plans are $199, $399 or $599 a month. What you pay for is the work you no longer do.
Pippit edits your clip when you ask, but its own page lists stock clips and music as tools you add.
Send VEXI the clips you shot and they come back cut, with B-roll, music and captions, sized for each platform.
Pippit's help center says it posts to TikTok, Facebook and Instagram.
VEXI posts to Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, Pinterest, Threads and your Google Business Profile.
The Publisher posts what you schedule. Its pages describe no mode that plans and posts the week on its own.
VEXI Autopilot runs your week ahead: it writes, cuts and posts, and can wait for your approval on everything.
Pippit's Trustpilot profile is rated 1.7. Some reviewers report credits taken by failed videos, refunds refused and plans cancelled the next day.
Edits your own footage: cuts, B-roll, music, captions
A broad AI toolbox from CapCut's maker, with a publisher for TikTok, Facebook and Instagram. You still run each tool and fill the calendar, and it does not plan the week for you.
One app: you ask, and it writes, designs, edits the video and posts it. Autopilot runs your week ahead.

Pippit is an AI creative tool that says it is "powered by CapCut". It makes videos from links and media, avatar and talking-photo videos and image designs, and it can schedule posts. Its site is pippit.ai.
Does Pippit post to social media?

Yes. Its help center says it posts to TikTok, Facebook and Instagram, on a schedule you set in its calendar. VEXI posts to Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, Pinterest, Threads and your Google Business Profile, and Autopilot can run the week.
Can Pippit edit my own videos?
Yes, in part: you upload a clip and type the change you want, and you add stock clips, music and captions with its tools. VEXI edits your footage for you: cuts, B-roll, music and captions.

There is a no-cost tier with daily credits. Paid plans (Starter, Plus and Pro) are sold by monthly credits. Third-party guides report different prices by country and promotion, so check its pricing page before you buy.
What do Trustpilot reviewers say about Pippit?
Pippit's Trustpilot profile is rated 1.7. Some reviewers report failed videos that still took credits, refunds refused, and a plan cancelled the day after paying.
